raw_comment:
**What do you notice?** 
Taylor Swift has more albums that have gone platinum in comparison to Michael Jackson, although Jackson's albums have overall more platinum certifications. Jackson's “Thriller” went platinum 34 times, while Swifts album with the most times platinum is “Fearless,” with 10 times.  Jackson's first four albums never went platinum, and five of Swift's albums are not counted due to their recent releases, or re-recorded nature that does not allow them to be counted in this way. Both artists have five albums that have crossed the threshold of five times platinum. 

**What Do I Wonder?**
I wonder what the differences in how music is released these days affects these numbers, and in what way. Jackson's music was not released in a time of streaming services, and Swift's was. Swift sels physical music, but that was the main form of sales and streams in Jackson's days. I wonder what this graph would look like if both of these Pop icons were releasing music at the same time. 

**How Does This Relate to Me and My Community?**
In their own ways, both of these artists help define their generation of music. Being someone who is interested in the present music industry, and would say Taylor Swift is one of the most impactful artists currently, it is interesting to see the comparison of just how huge Michael Jackson's albums were/are and the drastic impact he has had.

**Catchy Headline for the Graph**
Platinum Success of Albums for Two Pop Icons

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
While Taylor Swift has more platinum albums than Michael Jackson, Jackson's total number of platinum awards exceeds Swift's, according to the current data in the chart. Notably, most of Jackson's albums achieved platinum status more frequently than Swift's. This suggests that, despite the lower quantity, the impact of his albums is greater in terms of platinum achievements. However, with Swift's new albums not yet reviewed, it's possible that her total platinum awards could surpass Jackson's.

What do you wonder? 
It would be interesting to compare their platinum awards over a specific time, say a decade. Jackson's era lacked digital streaming, meaning his platinum sales were solely reliant on physical album sales. In contrast, artists today benefit from streaming services making it easier to achieve +1M sales. This raises important questions about how shifts in music engagement can influence artists’ platinum achievements.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This illustrates how music industry success is quantified over time. Both Jackson and Swift are iconic artists, yet their journeys to platinum success differ significantly due to technological shifts; the shift from physical album sales to digital streaming has streamlined the path to achieving platinum status, allowing artists today to reach significant platinum levels more easily than in the past.

How Technology Influences Platinum Success for Michael Jackson and Taylor Swift

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
From his ten solo albums, Michael Jackson has earned 72 platinum certifications. Thriller, his most popular album, has been certified 34 times platinum, solidifying its position as one of the most successful albums ever. Taylor Swift currently has 50 platinum certifications from 11 original albums but is projected to soon have about 90 platinum certifications. 

What Do I Wonder?
How have these figures changed as a result of the transition from CDs and vinyl to digital streaming? Does Swift have an advantage because digital music is easier and more accessible for people to stream? Would Michael Jackson have more platinum certifications if streaming had existed in his era? 

How Does This Relate to Me and My Community?
The music industry is constantly evolving and this comparison shows how streaming has transformed the way an artist's success is measured. Living and going to school in a city like New York, where the entertainment industry is a huge part of the culture, understanding these trends can help explain why artists market their music differently now. The Swift's Eras Tour had a massive economic impact on cities, in the hospitality industry especially, with economists even calling it "swiftonomics." 

Catchy Headline for the Graph
"Taylor Swift vs. Michael Jackson: The Platinum Battle Between Two Generations of Pop Legends"

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that Michael Jackson's "Thriller" significantly outsold his other albums by approximately 3 to 4 times his second and third most successful albums. I also notice that Michael Jackson's most  successful albums outsold Taylor Swift's most successful albums. I notice that the sales gradually descend following both artist's most popular/successful album. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder why "Thriller" significantly outsold his other albums. What was going on in the moment and how were people feeling? What is the context? What was the state of music or the music industry at the time?  What made this album resonate so much with listeners? How has the album sold over time to accumulate so many sales? Did majority of the sales occur the time of release or has the album consistently sold well? Why haven't Taylor's later albums sold as well as her earlier albums? Is its related to the change in the way we consume music with streaming? Is it the quality of the music? Is it over saturation? What about the preferences of listeners? 

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community in the sense that I am a part of the generation that has lived to consume both Taylor and Michael Jackson. Taylor is the moment and Michael Jackson is a generational talent and icon. I am not a huge fan of Taylor Swift, but I respect her art. The older I get, the more I appreciate Michael Jackson. 

Battle of Generational Icons

raw_comment:
What stands out most in this graph is the difference between Taylor Swift's and Michael Jackson's approaches to achieving platinum records. Thriller by Michael Jackson took a few years to reach platinum status and is the number one song with 34 platinum certifications. Taylor Swift, on the other hand, experienced instant popularity after her debut album went platinum, and up until a recent decline, her albums usually had high certifications. This graph raises questions to me about how Taylor Swift's certifications would be if her new albums that she recorded again were included and if they were as popular as the originals. Both Taylor Swift and Micheal Jackson are very well known in my community by all ages and it's interesting to see the effects they have side by side on the graph.
My headline is "Thriller vs. Taylor: Platinum certifications"

raw_comment:
- I notice that the graph highlights Taylor Swift's current dominance, particularly in the 2020s, where her music has consistently topped the charts, breaking records. It seems that her fanbase is not just vast but deeply engaged, as her albums continue to generate huge amounts of streams and sales. In contrast, Michael Jackson's peak was more spread out over time, with hits like Thriller in the '80s that defined an entire era.
-  I wonder how much streaming platforms and social media influence today’s music scene. Taylor Swift’s success seems to be amplified by platforms like Spotify, TikTok, and Instagram, which allow her to maintain a constant presence and interaction with fans. In comparison, Michael Jackson didn’t have access to these tools, so I’m curious how his career might have been different had he been able to use modern social media for promotion and fan interaction.
- In my community, Taylor Swift has a massive presence—her albums are the soundtrack to many people's lives, especially among younger generations. Her music often brings people together at school events, parties, and in social media conversations. Michael Jackson's influence is still present too, especially with iconic songs that are part of the cultural fabric, but Taylor Swift feels more immediate to my peers. 
-  A headline to capture the graph’s idea is Swift vs. Jackson: A “Thriller” and “Fearless” Race to be at the Top of Pop Royalty.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I noticed that Michael Jackson’s Thriller has a huge number of platinum certifications—34—while Taylor Swift’s highest is 10. That’s a big difference, and it shows how much longer Thriller has been popular. I also realized that the chart doesn’t show Taylor Swift’s most recent album sales, so her total could actually be higher.

What do you wonder?
I wonder if Taylor Swift could eventually get as many platinum certifications as Michael Jackson with her newer albums that aren’t shown in the graph. I also wonder how much the amount of time they’ve been making music affects their total platinum certifications. Michael Jackson’s career has lasted a lot longer than Taylor Swift’s, so maybe that’s why he has more certifications.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This shows how an artist’s influence can last over time. Michael Jackson’s high number of platinum certifications probably means people are still listening to his music even though it came out years ago. Taylor Swift is still a newer artist, so she hasn’t had as much time to reach that level of success yet. In my community, a lot of people still listen to Michael Jackson, which shows how an artist’s music can stay popular for a long time.

raw_comment:
Graphs show the achievements of Michael Jackson compared to Taylor Swift, in terms of album certifications in platinum. Jackson's Thriller stands out with a record 34 platinum certifications, which is really historic in records. Swift has a more even buildup in the certifications for her albums, and by the projections shown, her certifications are likely to pass Jackson's total soon given her continued release and re-recordings.

The Grammy-similar graph shows that while Swift has fewer wins than Beyoncé and others, her nominations within key categories are strong acknowledgements of her artistry. That lends some credence to the notion that sales are not necessarily defining "the best."

Is it likely that Taylor Swift will ever pass Jackson in overall certifications throughout all her albums?
How does the switch in model from physical album sales during Jackson's time to streaming sales in Swift's time affect their overall certification totals? Do Grammy wins and nominations matter for a matric of;Legacy?

This speaks to the conversations that happen with the shifting metrics of success in music-from physical album sales to streaming and digital downloads. This also shows how generations of artists redefine success. In my community, we debate what defines a great artist: is it cultural impact, longevity, or accolades like Grammys?

"Michael Jackson vs. Taylor Swift: A Platinum Legacy Across Generations"

raw_comment:
What stands out most in this graph is the difference between Taylor Swift's and Michael Jackson's approaches to achieving platinum records. Thriller by Michael Jackson took a few years to reach platinum status and is the number one song with 34 platinum certifications. Taylor Swift, on the other hand, experienced instant popularity after her debut album went platinum, and up until a recent decline, her albums usually had high certifications. This graph raises questions to me about how Taylor Swift's certifications would be if her new albums that she recorded again were included and if they were as popular as the originals. Both Taylor Swift and Micheal Jackson are very well known in my community by all ages and it's interesting to see the effects they have side by side on the graph.
My headline is "Thriller vs. Taylor: Platinum certifications"

raw_comment: * What stands out to me the most about the graph is that in Micheal Jacksons career, his first four years didn’t award him a platinum but once he made a successful song it led to many breakthrough records and many platinum awards. In contrast Taylor Swift won platinums from the first album displayed in the chart, and only began to not win or see a decrease in number of platinums after being very successful. Some questions the graph posed for me, were why Micheal Jackson’s ‘Thriller’ is in blue, while two of Taylor Swift’s albums appear in color, when they only won platinum 9 and 10 times, and Micheal Jackson has another album that has won more than 10 times. raw_comment:
I see that MJ’s ‘Thriller’ album has done best out of all of him and Taylors albums; however, most of his albums seem to have higher lines on the graph than Taylors. I think it has to do with things that are opinion based.

Relatability: Michael Jackson’s music (in my opinion) caters to a wider audience with his songs that are nostalgic to some people that grew up in the 80s, or with his songs about injustice in the world such as ‘Scream’ and ‘Earth Song.’ Taylor on the other hand has a more female and younger fanbase, and yes, it’s a very big one, but her music is catered towards that audience. 

The Fanbases: Earlier I mentioned how Michael Jacksons fans are probably a lot older, and Taylors is younger and more female oriented. Another issue is how the fans react. I rarely ever see any MJ fans on TikTok, Twitter or even Instagram, but when it comes to Taylor, I only ever see negative things about either her (that non-fans say) or the insane things that the very odd Taylor fans say when people don’t like her. People say her fanbase is more ‘cult’ like due to the mass amounts of people at concerts and their behavior, but with MJ people just prefer to enjoy the music.

At the end of the day, comparing music artists that are successful is I feel like something that doesn’t need to be such a big problem that people make it out to be. You like what you like, a lot of stuff is opinion based, and music is subjective and means something different to everyone.

raw_comment: I noticed that the best-selling album for Taylor Swift is her Fearless album, and the best-selling album for Micheal Jackson is his Thiller album. However, Taylor Swift has a close second album that went platinum 9 times called 1989. Both of them are her best- selling albums so far. I also noticed that the bar graph for Micheal Jackson’s best-selling album, Thriller overwhelmingly exceeded the bar graph for Taylor Swift’s album, Fearless. I wonder if Taylor Swift can still be more popular than Micheal Jackson even though his album went platinum 34 times while Taylor Swift’s album went platinum 10 times. This relates to my community and I because a greater number of adults talk about Micheal Jackson and his music than Taylor Swift and her music. On the other hand, Taylor Swift appeals more to the younger generations causing her to be more popular among young adults, teens, and children. Since Taylor Swift is still actively releasing music, she can experiment with new genres and appeal to more people of different age groups. This can increase the number of albums she sells and could one day, surpass Jackson’s 34 platinum record. A headline to capture the graph’s idea is Swift vs. Jackson: A “Thriller” and “Fearless” Race to be at the Top of Pop Royalty.

raw_comment:
While Taylor Swift has many fans and is often praised for her talent and contributions to music, there are some criticisms that her detractors mention. People who argue that she should be "canceled" may point to a few key issues:

Some critics have accused Swift of appropriating aspects of different cultures in her music videos and performances, suggesting that she doesn't always give appropriate credit or context.

Swift has had several high-profile feuds, most notably with Kanye West and Katy Perry. Some people view her responses to these conflicts as dramatic or overly sensationalized, which can turn fans and observers against her.

Initially, Swift was criticized for her perceived silence on political issues. Although she has become more vocal recently, some feel that her late involvement is disingenuous or should have come sooner.

Critics sometimes argue that her carefully curated image and the marketing of her personal life can come off as manipulative or inauthentic, leading to disillusionment among fans.

 Some people feel that Swift often portrays herself in a victim light, which can rub others the wrong way, especially when it comes to her breakups and public disputes.

These points reflect some opinions held by critics, and it's essential to remember that views about public figures can vary widely. Many fans still deeply admire her for her music and personal growth over the years.

raw_comment:
Why Some People Think Taylor Swift's Music Lacks Depth

Taylor Swift is a famous artist, but not everyone enjoys her music. Some believe her songs lack depth for a few reasons.

 1. Similar Songwriting

Critics say Swift's songs often follow the same pattern, focusing on love and heartbreak. This repetition can make her music predictable and less exciting.

 2. Focus on Sales

Some think her commercial success prioritizes profits over art. The music industry pressures artists to create hits, which can reduce the emotional depth of her songs.

#### 3. Lyric Simplicity

While many fans like her storytelling, some find her lyrics too simple. Critics argue that she uses clichés, making her songs feel more like diary entries than deep emotional explorations.

#### 4. **Shift to Pop*

Swift transitioned from country to pop music, and some fans miss the authenticity of her earlier work. This shift can make it harder for certain listeners to connect with her new songs.

#### 5. **Too Much Exposure**

With social media and streaming, some feel overwhelmed by her constant releases. This overexposure can lead to listener fatigue, making it harder to engage with her music.



Though Taylor Swift has many fans and is influential in the music industry, there are valid critiques about her music's depth. Factors like similar songwriting, a focus on sales, simple lyrics, her shift to pop, and overexposure contribute to the belief that her music may not resonate with everyone.

- **Annotated bar chart / column chart**
- It compares album **platinum certifications** across albums for two artists.

- **Side-by-side panels** for two artists (**Michael Jackson** and **Taylor Swift**), functioning like **small multiples / faceting by artist**.
- Within each panel, bars are shown in **chronological order** by album.
- **Color highlighting** is used to emphasize specific albums (blue for *Thriller*, pink for *Fearless* and *1989*).
- Not stacked.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Artist | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into left/right panels; text labels |
| Album | Categorical/nominal | Individual bars/marks; album name labels for selected albums |
| Album chronological order | Ordinal | Position along x-axis within each artist panel |
| Platinum certifications | Quantitative | Bar height / position on y-axis |
| Highlighted album status (selected albums) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of bars (blue/pink vs gray) |

raw_comment:
I notice how Michael Jackson seems to have significantly more platinum times for his albums, with his highest, Thriller, gaining more than 3 times as many as Taylor Swift’s best, Fearless.
I wonder if Platinum Times is a worthy indicator of an album or artists. When Michael Jackson ran the pop industry, streaming services such as Spotify and Apple Music didn’t exist. YouTube was not widely used to listen to music, prompting radio networks and physical albums to be the primary source of music entertainment. Another indicator of this is how while Michael Jackson has better Album sales, Taylor has significantly more streams and in-person concert viewers. While these are both affected by their time, we can tell that they have relatively similar musical success based on their Grammy count, 13 and 14 respectively. This proves that album sales in the form of Platinum Times aren’t a worthy indicator of an album’s success.
This relates to me and my community, as music is a soulful entertainment, and art that brings people together. Using it to teach us about improperly represented conclusions based on outdated or irrelevant data is so inspiring.
“Taylor might run the music industry now, but the king of pop will always be platinum.”

I wonder how Michael Jackson was able to achieve such popularity in an era with less availability for advertisements, whereas Taylor Swift would theoretically have an easier time gaining more popularity with the widespread use of the internet.

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that this graph compares two of the world's biggest pop stars, the late Micheal Jackson and Taylor Swift, based on the number of platinum certifications they have accumulated throughout their career. Micheal Jackson has an overwhelming lead, with his top album, "Thriller," earning  24 more platinum certifications than Swift's top album, "Fearless." It is important to note that the certifications for Swift's rereleased albums are not up-to-date, and, therefore, this graph is not entirely accurate. It is interesting how Jackson's first four albums did not receive nearly as much attention as his later ones. Taylor Swift has released more albums than Micheal Jackson, yet none have achieved the same amount of fame as "Thriller."
2. I wonder if the stark difference between Thriller and Fearless is due to Thriller being out for a longer. I wonder if this gap will close as time goes by. Would Taylor's rerecorded albums come closer to the certifications of Thriller if they were up-to-date? 
3. This is relevant to me because Micheal Jackson and Taylor Swift are two artists that I love and have made major waves in the music industry. Their music has shifted the popular culture, forever changing music trends. I have witnessed many claims that Taylor is the new "Queen of Pop" replacing Micheal Jackson, but I think this graph proves them wrong.
4. Timeless vs. Trending: Comparing Two Icons' Platinum Legacies

raw_comment: One thing I notice about this graph is the fact that Michael Jackson’s ‘Thriller’ album is 2 times greater in platinum certifications than Taylor Swift’s ‘Fearless’ album. I find this difference very interesting because the beginning of indie pop, (taylor swift’s primary genre) was not very far away from the release of the thriller album being that the genre began in the late 70’s. One thing this leads me to wonder is whether disco and classic rock would still hold the same weight/popularity as thriller once did assuming a musician released a similar album today? This relates to me mostly because music is a big part of my life and seeing how successful artists can get from producing something unique as well as the emotional connection I am able to have with particular songs. If I could give this graphic a headline, I would call it “Platinum Race; Indie pop and Classic rock.”

- **Color highlighting** is used to emphasize specific albums (blue for *Thriller*, pink for *Fearless* and *1989*).
- Not stacked.

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Artist | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into left/right panels; text labels |
| Album | Categorical/nominal | Individual bars/marks; album name labels for selected albums |
| Album chronological order | Ordinal | Position along x-axis within each artist panel |
| Platinum certifications | Quantitative | Bar height / position on y-axis |
| Highlighted album status (selected albums) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of bars (blue/pink vs gray) |

raw_comment:
This graph shows the number of platinum certifications, or 1,000,000 streams/albums, that each album by Michael Jackson and Taylor Swift has. These albums are ordered chronologically from left to right. I notice that Thriller by Micheal Jackson is a clear outlier in this graph, with an astonishingly high number of over 30 Platinum certifications. Additionally, I noticed that the first four of Michael Jackson’s albums did not earn any platinum and then he suddenly released Thriller, and the album before Thriller which both earned more than 5 platinum. This is in contrast to Taylor Swift, who earned more than 5 platinum on her debut album. I think this might show that Taylor Swift had more talent than Michael Jackson but Michael Jackson was able to develop his talent better to produce Thriller, one of the best-selling albums of all time. On top of this, the last few albums produced by Taylor Swift didn’t earn any Platinums. 

2) I wonder if this might show that Taylor Swift had more talent than Michael Jackson but Michael Jackson was able to develop his talent better to produce Thriller, one of the best-selling albums of all time. 

Additionally, I wonder if Taylor Swift has passed her musical peak. because her past three albums have earned 0 platinum total and her peak album was almost 16 years ago with the album “Fearless”. In comparison, Michael Jackson was much more consistent throughout his career, aside from the exception of Thriller, which is a definite outlier.

raw_comment:
Headline: The Platinum Race: Will Taylor Swift Catch Up?
What do I notice?
I notice that Michael Jackson’s Thriller album has far more platinum certifications than any of Taylor Swift's albums. Thriller has reached 34 platinum certifications, while Taylor’s highest albums, Fearless and 1989, have 10 and 9. The graph also shows that Taylor’s newer re-recorded albums haven’t had their platinum counts updated yet.
What do I wonder?
How does Thriller compare to other famous albums in terms of platinum certifications? I’m also curious if Taylor Swift’s re-recorded albums will eventually reach similar levels. Additionally, I wonder if changes in the music industry have made it easier or harder for more modern albums to succeed. 
What do I think is going on in this graph?
This graph compares the success of Michael Jackson and Taylor Swift’s albums by looking at their platinum certifications. It shows how Thriller’s big success has been, even compared to a world-renowned artist like Taylor Swift.
How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community because everyone listens to music and especially these artists. My parents listen to Michael Jackson's music, and my sisters and I are Taylor Swift fans.

raw_comment:
In this graph, they are showing the albums released by both Taylor Swift and Michael Jackson and showing how many times those albums have gone platinum. I noticed that Thriller reached 34 platinum certifications. However, none of his other albums are even close to that number. I also noticed that, on the contrary, all of Taylor Swift's albums are relatively close together. I wonder two main things. First, is it better to have one big album and a bunch of others that did well, OR is it better to have a bunch of albums that all performed well and not one huge one? I'm also curious about what made the album Thriller so popular. This is extremely relevant to me as I have been a huge fan of both performers since I was little, so it is extremely interesting to see them being compared. It is also relevant because the success of Taylor Swift has been a huge discussion in the media today, so it is even more interesting to see her put against such a monumental music figure like Michael Jackson.

raw_comment:
Headline: Is Taylor Swift really as popular as it seems? 
I notice that Michael Jackson's “Thriller” album has no more platinum certifications compared to Taylor Swift's top albums (Fearless and 1989). I also notice that the majority of other Michael Jackson albums also have more platinum certification than the majority of Taylor Swifts. I also notice that platinum albums are defined as albums that have sold 1,000,000 copies. It also mentions Taylor Swift's recent sales data was not included in this demographic. I wonder if these things could have skewed the results. Although it does say a certain amount of online streaming of songs does count as a copy sold, that doesn't seem to be an accurate, definite way to measure compared to a copy being sold. Looking at Taylor Swift's popularity, this graph may be trying to show this isn't an accurate way to measure popularity. Although Michael Jackson has more albums sold, especially in the modern generation, there is no doubt Taylor Swift is "bigger.”. Her popularity is shown through more modern ways like Instagram and TikTok following. This relates to me and my community because Taylor is a very big part of my community. There are very few people in my generation that would be able to name specific Michael Jackson songs or names of his albums. Though almost everyone in my generation, even people who don't listen to Taylor Swift, are able to name some of her songs and albums. Almost everyone loves and listens to her.

raw_comment:
Headlines: Two Artists on the Top: Michael Jackson and Taylor Swift's Top Platinum Records
The graph depicts a comparison between Taylor Swift and Michael Jackson. It shows the difference between Jackson's and Swift's platinum records.  One thing I noticed from the graph is that Taylor Swift's most successful records are "Fearless" with ten platinum records, and "1989" with nine platinum records. However, Micheal Jackson's "Thriller" has more than 3 times the amount of platinum records than Taylor Swift's "Fearless." Also, Jackson's first four albums did not go platinum at all. One thing I wonder is if Taylor Swift's album, which has not been certified yet, could pass "Thriller." Another question I have is why "Thriller" is so much more popular compared to Jackson's other albums and Taylor Swift's albums. This chart relates to me because I love Taylor Swift, and she is very popular among girls my age. I like to see her compared to other artists. It is interesting to see how successful Micheal Jackson is compared to her. I never really understood how popular he was when he was in his prime, and now I can understand.

Some people in my community (including me) love Michael Jackson, love Taylor Swift, and love both. The only relation is that we contributed to the graph by buying and streaming their albums.

Two Pop Artists, Two Different Eras

raw_comment:
In today's graph, I notice that Michael Jackson and Taylor Swift's music albums are being compared based on platinum certifications. Michael Jackson has a large number of platinum certifications on his album “Thriller” (being platinum 34 times). This is a much larger number compared to Taylor Swift, whose highest number of platinum certifications is 10. This shows that Michael Jackson's album is very successful and popular. I wonder what made Michael Jackson's "Thriller" album, so popular, compared to his other albums which weren't as successful (did not receive as many platinum certifications). I also wonder if the reason Taylor Swift's albums aren't reaching so many platinum certifications is due to her having so many albums being produced, which lessens the focus on one album gaining ultimate success. This relates to me and my community because pop culture and music plays a huge part in society today, and it shows how much people stream and listen to these popular artists, and what causes each artist to gain platinum certifications.

raw_comment:
The first thing that I noticed was Michael Jackson's outstanding "Thriller" album, coming in at 34 times platinum.  Michael Jackson is said to be the greatest pop artist of all time, while Taylor Swift is said to be the greatest pop artist of the current music industry.  I noticed that Swift's most sold album, "Fearless," only reached 10 platinum certifications, compared to Jackson's outstanding 34 platinum certifications.  Michael Jackson's album has been platinum certified three times as much as Swift's most popular album, "Fearless."  While a vast majority of the younger generations will argue that Taylor Swift is the greatest pop musician of all time, it is clear that Michael Jackson has dominated the pop industry solely based on his "Thriller" album.  I also notice that Swift's "Taylor's Version" albums have not yet been certified, and Jackson's first four albums are not platinum.  I wonder if Taylor Swift's existing albums will ever come close to Jackson's "Thriller," or if she will release an album in the future that will send the album's platinum certifications soaring. What do you notice?
I notice that Michael Jackson has a large number of platinum certifications on his album “Thriller”, being platinum 34 times. This is much more compared to Taylor Swift whose highest number of platinum certifications is 10. It doesn’t account for her most recent album sales.

What do you wonder?
I wonder if Taylor Swift could reach the same number of platinum certifications with her newer albums that aren't recorded in the graph. How has the amount of time they have made music impacted their platinum certifications?

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to how much impact a figure in pop culture has over time. The reason why Michael Jackson has so many platinum certifications is likely because people still listen to his music that was released years or even decades ago. Taylor Swift doesn’t reach that metric since she is a more recent artist and has had less time to reach that level of success.

Platinum: The Legacy of Pop Icons

I notice that that the album that Micheal Jackson created,  Thriller, has the longest bar that exceeds the bar graph more than Taylor Swift's biggest album Fearless. I also notice that Micheal Jackson has gotten 30 Platinum certifications on this, while Fearless only has nearly 10. I also notice that Micheal Jackson's first four albums are not platinum, while Taylor Swift's first 9 were platinum. I wonder if any of Taylor Swifts albums in the future will exceed Micheal Jackson's album thriller in platinum certifications? I also wonder how many listens that Micheal Jackson's album still gets daily? I wonder if Taylor Swift's new album "The Tortured Poets Department" is growing as great as the album Thriller since it's becoming very popular. I think that in the graph, there is a comparison between Micheal Jackson's albums and Taylor Swift's albums and how many platinum certifications that it received, if any at all. I also think that in the graph, they are drastically showing the greatest hit album of both artists and emphasizing that Micheal Jackson's album is still so much more popular off of platinum certifications of 30, that it would be very hard to overcome this number. This relates to me and my community because of the attention that Taylor Swift is receiving, and how popular she is. This also reveals how Micheal Jackson is remembered for his great album that we still listen to today.

raw_comment:
A Battle of Platinum Giants: Thriller vs. Taylor Swift’s Top Hits

I noticed that Michael Jackson’s Thriller holds an extraordinary 34 platinum certifications, and his other albums also reached high certification levels, on par with some of Taylor Swift’s best-performing albums. Swift’s recent re-releases, however, are missing certifications, possibly due to their newer status. Overall, Michael Jackson’s career appears slightly more successful, with Thriller creating his iconic status. Although, Taylor Swift’s career is still progressing with consistently platinum albums. I wonder how including Taylor’s newest releases would affect the graph and if streaming services are factored into these certifications, as Jackson’s achievements would be even more impressive without the reach of platforms like Spotify. In my community, Taylor Swift is more popular at school, though Michael Jackson’s music seems more universally accepted.

raw_comment:
On first glance, I notice that Michael Jackson's "Thriller" album seems to be some sort of anomaly.  It appears to triple his previous album, and his following album goes back down into where I'd assume it to be.  I also notice that is states that Taylor Swift's platinum certifications are not up to date, but even then, I believe they won't amount to Jackson's level of notoriety.

I wonder why Thriller did as well as it did.  I understand how enjoyable it is to listen to, as Thriller is an incredible song.  My only assumption would be that because it is used on the holidays (and frequently played on repeat), it acts as a universally enjoyable song, used by everyone participating in Halloween, whether or not they share the same music tastes as one another outside of the holiday itself.

While a song like this doesn't really affect my community in a massive way, I have been to many a Hallow's Eve party and noticed people enjoying their time spent with their closest companions, most of the time with Thriller in the background.  I see Thriller as being a song in which entire communities can find refuge in, and I'd like to think that bonds can be made because of a catchy song playing in the background of a party where one guy is dressed up as Where's Waldo, and another guy is dressed up as a Zombie.

raw_comment:
Noticed: I noticed that Michael Jackson’s first four albums weren’t platinum, whereas Taylor Swift’s first nine albums were all platinum. However, due to Michael’s success with 34 times platinum on Thriller, his overall number of platinums is very similar to Taylor’s. They are also closer now as Taylor Swift has only had one platinum album in her last 6 albums. Michael Jackson also has 10 albums compared to Taylor’s 15. 
Wonder: I wonder how current trends and recency bias are affecting the popularity of the two artists’ albums. Michael Jackson started out slow, but gained popularity quickly, whereas Taylor Swift started off strong, but recently has been losing some traction. Taylor’s gradual loss of popularity could be due to a bandwagon effect where she was consistently popular because everyone was listening to her, or it could be because other artists are releasing music and there isn’t enough to go around. I think Michael Jackson’s case was different as he didn’t release as many albums, which makes the listeners more eager for each new album. 
Community: This relates to my community and I as Michael Jackson and Taylor Swift are very well known throughout. It is common to hear their songs on the radio, and many people regard both artists very highly. The graph reflects their status as both have sold millions of copies throughout many different albums.

image_description:
## 1) Chart type
- **Annotated bar chart / column chart**
- It compares album **platinum certifications** across albums for two artists.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Side-by-side panels** for two artists (**Michael Jackson** and **Taylor Swift**), functioning like **small multiples / faceting by artist**.
- Within each panel, bars are shown in **chronological order** by album.
- **Color highlighting** is used to emphasize specific albums (blue for *Thriller*, pink for *Fearless* and *1989*).
- Not stacked.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Artist | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into left/right panels; text labels |
| Album | Categorical/nominal | Individual bars/marks; album name labels for selected albums |
| Album chronological order | Ordinal | Position along x-axis within each artist panel |
| Platinum certifications | Quantitative | Bar height / position on y-axis |
| Highlighted album status (selected albums) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of bars (blue/pink vs gray) |
raw_comment:
When looking at this graph, the first thing I noticed was the obvious disparity between the highest platinum album from Michael Jackson and the highest platinum album from Taylor Swift. After a further inspection, it is seen that Taylor Swift has more total albums with the title of platinum, but the amount of times platinum is less than Michael Jackson’s fewer albums. Another noticeable detail is the fact that while Michael’s first albums were not platinum, Taylor’s latest albums have been the ones not to receive the award.
It makes me wonder how the success of an artist can be seen through their platinum albums, and if this directly correlates to the popularity of artists, such as Taylor Swift and Michael Jackson's success. The graph shows the rough numbers of sales, and based on what seems to be trends, I wonder how future fanbases would have received albums that Michael Jackson could have released, and how sales would have performed. 
This chart helps to explain parts of the music industry, such as how all musicians eventually reach a peak time in their career, although some last longer than others. For my peers and community around me this can help those who want to pursue a career in music and even those who do not, proving the idea of never giving up, as shown with the first few albums of Michael Jackson’s career not being hits, but after much work and commitment, eventually succeeded past what was ever seen before.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that Michael Jackson has a large number of platinum certifications on his album “Thriller”, being platinum 34 times. This is much more compared to Taylor Swift whose highest number of platinum certifications is 10. It doesn’t account for her most recent album sales.

What do you wonder?
I wonder if Taylor Swift could reach the same number of platinum certifications with her newer albums that aren't recorded in the graph. How has the amount of time they have made music impacted their platinum certifications?

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to how much impact a figure in pop culture has over time. The reason why Michael Jackson has so many platinum certifications is likely because people still listen to his music that was released years or even decades ago. Taylor Swift doesn’t reach that metric since she is a more recent artist and has had less time to reach that level of success.

Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
Platinum: The Legacy of Pop Icons

|---|---|---|

It shocks me how big of a gap there is between Micheal Jackson and Taylor Swift, especially with her recent burst in popularity. Another statistic that shocks me is how Taylor Swift is losing sales of albums even after gaining popularity. The giant gap and loss of sales are explainable though since the number of people using album records in the 20th century has dwindled, and Micheal Jackson is a dead artist and is titled the “King of Pop” which explains his overwhelming popularity.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice This Graph is showing statistics regarding music, and awards given from each artist. Michael Jackson has significantly more Platinum Certifications than taylor swift does. Michael Jackson's "Thriller" has 34 platinums while Taylor swift's "Fearless" has 10. Platinum Certifications are per every 1,000,000 people downloading music. This shows that michael Jackson's music so far has beat taylor swift swiftly. 
What do you wonder?
I wonder If the different ways people download and listen to this music has affected the results. For example, now we can listen to music for free, and on the radio. For Michael Jackson, people may have had to buy albums more often causing an incline in the "streams" of his music. I also wonder if the time period of these musicians has affected the results. 
How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community because people around me, and myself listen to these artists everyday. Our habits to turn on either Taylor Swift or Michael Jackson has affected this graph in some way.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that both Micheal Jackson and Taylor Swift have the same number of total platinum albums. However, Jackson has more total platinum certifications than Swift as a result of Jackson’s “Thriller.” Swift’s biggest album “Fearless,” is only 10 times platinum in comparison to Jackson’s “Thriller” which is 34 times platinum. 


What do you wonder?
I wonder what caused Micheal Jackson’s “Thriller” to blow up to become 34 times platinum. I also wonder why Jackson’s first four albums did not reach platinum status. I am also curious as to why Taylor Swift’s albums have declined in platinum certification as she has released more music. What caused that?


How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because Micheal Jackson and Taylor Swift are both legends in the music industry. Like myself, most people my age have listened to both Micheal Jackson and Taylor Swift growing up. Swift is extremely revelevent and present in our daily lives and music choices. However, Jackson is a music icon, so I think that this graph could spark a lot of debates over who is the better musician.

Headline:
Why are Taylor Swift and Micheal Jackson So Popular?

When it comes to the world of music, Micheal Jackson and Taylor Swift are two incredibly talented and popular artists who have left a lasting impact on the industry. While both artists have their own unique style and fan base, Micheal Jackson is undeniably more popular than Taylor Swift.

What I noticed:
Michael Jackson and Taylor Swift are two of the most iconic artists in the music industry, even though Taylor Swift has made many platinum hits she is not even close to reaching Micheal Jackson's hits.

Why is Michael Jackson more popular than Taylor Swift?

Michael Jackson is often seen as more popular than Taylor Swift because he was a groundbreaking artist who changed the music industry with his unique style and amazing dance moves. His hits like "Thriller" and "Billie Jean" became iconic, and he had a huge impact on pop culture. While Taylor Swift is also incredibly talented and has a massive fan base, Michael's influence and legacy in music history are hard to match.

What do you notice? 
I notice that Thriller is exponentially higher than any other bar on the graph, but Taylor has more platinum albums. I also noticed that Michael’s albums were less popular in the beginning, while Taylor’s re-recordings do not have any data to jump off of. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder how long each of their careers has lasted. If the data were to be extrapolated to make their respective careers last the same amount of time, who would theoretically have a higher amount of platinum albums?

How does this relate to you and your community?

raw_comment:
WGOITG? Swift vs. Jackson
	I notice that Taylor Swift’s first albums were successful, whereas Michael Jackson’s first four albums didn’t even go Platinum. I also see that Thriller beats anything Taylor Swift has done by a huge amount. Thriller is one of the most successful albums of all time, not just between the two of them. Furthermore, Taylor Swift has a higher number of Platinum albums than Jackson does, so Taylor Swift has quantity, but Jackson has quality. 
	I wonder what made Thriller so much more successful than anything else, and I also wonder why Michael Jackson’s first few albums were not so successful. I also wonder why none of Swift’s albums have seen the same success as Thriller, because she’s certainly as well known as Michael Jackson was. 
	This relates to me and my community because Taylor Swift is one of my generation’s biggest stars, so it’s interesting to compare her to other stars from the past.

raw_comment:
I notice that this bar graph shows how Micheal Jackson’s number of streams compares with Taylor Swift’s. I was surprised to see that Swift’s most popular album looked insignificant to Jackson. Her albums, however, seem to be more consistent in the number of streams than Jackson. This is probably because of his fast rise to fame, while Swift has been steadily rising after her initial boost.

I wonder if it is possible to predict how this will change over time. I know that many of Taylor Swift’s albums, especially because she has rerecorded them, are lower in streams just because of how new they are. Over time, I wonder if hers will slowly begin to increase or catch up, although looking at Micheal Jackson’s stats, they probably will not reach that level. Additionally, do physical copies of albums over streams matter in this situation?

I love Taylor Swift’s music and I’ve definitely heard this argument about Jackson vs Swift multiple times, so this did immediately catch my interest.

raw_comment:
1) This graph shows the number of platinum certifications, or 1,000,000 streams/albums, that each album by Michael Jackson and Taylor Swift has. These albums are ordered chronologically from left to right. I notice that Thriller by Micheal Jackson is a clear outlier in this graph, with an astonishingly high number of over 30 Platinum certifications. Additionally, I noticed that the first four of Michael Jackson’s albums did not earn any platinum and then he suddenly released Thriller, and the album before Thriller which both earned more than 5 platinum. This is in contrast to Taylor Swift, who earned more than 5 platinum on her debut album. I think this might show that Taylor Swift had more talent than Michael Jackson but Michael Jackson was able to develop his talent better to produce Thriller, one of the best-selling albums of all time. On top of this, the last few albums produced by Taylor Swift didn’t earn any Platinums. 

2) I wonder if this might show that Taylor Swift had more talent than Michael Jackson but Michael Jackson was able to develop his talent better to produce Thriller, one of the best-selling albums of all time. 

Additionally, I wonder if Taylor Swift has passed her musical peak. because her past three albums have earned 0 platinum total and her peak album was almost 16 years ago with the album “Fearless”. In comparison, Michael Jackson was much more consistent throughout his career, aside from the exception of Thriller, which is a definite outlier.

What do you wonder?
I wonder what factors made Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” earn so many awards compared to Taylor Swift’s. Her highest can’t compare to his. I wonder if this was the time the music was released or the popularity beforehand. I wonder how Micahel Jackson’s “Thriller” album would have done if it had been released now, and Taylor Swift’s then. 

How does this relate to you and your community?
I know personally Michael Jackson relates a lot to me because my uncle used to play his music a lot growing up. My parents were teenagers when “Thriller” came out and they always put on Michael Jackson’s music when they pick what we should listen to. Taylor Swift has a big relation to our community, specifically Santa Clara. I know Taylor Swift came to perform at Levi’s Stadium right here in my city. She boosted our economy so much because so many people went to go see her. She was officially mayor for a day and the town was even named “Swiftie Clara” that day.

What do you notice?
I notice that Thriller has been certified platinum 34 different times! This is higher than Taylor Swift’s biggest album, Fearless, by 24 platinum awards which is 24 million more sales! 

What do you wonder?
I wonder why Thriller was so popular for Michael Jackson? His previous album was very successful too with 9 respective platinum awards, but how come Michael Jackson all of the sudden became insanely popular, getting 34 platinum awards on his next album, Thriller?

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because it shows how big the music industry actually is. A platinum award is given to an album when it reaches 1 million sales. This shows the popularity of music in everyone’s lives by showing two of the biggest music creators of all time.

3. Title- Michael Jackson v.s Taylor Swift: The Ultimate Pop Showdown

I wonder if Michael Jackson's albums have more platinum certifications than Taylor Swift's music because Michael Jackson was popular earlier than Taylor Swift was, so his music was around longer that hers.
